NEW MEXICAN
Santa Fe, New Mexico
December 28, 1954

Will Power

We see where a factory owner has offered $100 cash
to any employe who will swear off smoking and keep his
pledge throughout 1955. With all of the stories circulating
inking lung. cancer to cigarettes and heart ailments tc
cigars, we think it takes more will power to keep on smok-
ing than it does to stop.
Almost everyone knows some person who swore of!
during the year, We've put up with their newly-kindlec
tempers and, when they're feeling particularly bad, witk
their supercilious superior airs. We've seen them smirk at
the hospitable offer of a cigarette, and we've heard them
dismiss their host with a vinegar-dripping, “No, I GAVE
IT UP"—loud enough for everybody in the room to hear.
We've seen these same self-centered individuals,
whose physical appearance had been spare and lithe and
rd as nails, turn soft, developing gradually increasing
orporations” from their constant plea: “Anybody have
any candy?”
We've heard their frequent references to how much
money the've saved during the year. That is, how much
money they haven't spent on cigarettes, because for some
reason the money hasn't been saved—we still are called
upon to lend a dollar or so for lunch,
We've seen all this and have decided we'll stick with
It for a while. And one of our friends, who took the pledge
some months ago, says he’s so sick of the company he has
to keep as a “‘smoker anonymous” that his New Year's
resolution will be to stop not smoking.
